newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Denway seeks road ahead for GZ Peugeot.
newsitem.headline: Denway seeks road ahead for GZ Peugeot.

text.p: Denway Investment Ltd said it will hold discussions with PSA Peugeot Citroen to hammer out a plan to buoy their loss-making China automobile joint venture, Vice Managing Director Sam Pan said on Wednesday.
"French Peugeot has several officials in Guangzhou preparing to set up a shareholders meeting," Pan told a news briefing, adding he hoped a meeting could be held next month.
Denway, a listed arm of the Guangzhou municipal government, has an 46 percent interest in Guangzhou Peugeot Automobile Co Ltd. France's Peugeot had 22 percent as at year end.
Earlier on Wednesday, Denway announced an interim net loss of HK$75.76 million, 30 percent more than the previous year.
Some HK$61.04 million of the loss was from associaties, mainly Guangzhou Peugeot.
Pan said the automobile maker, badly hit by oversupply and China's tight marcoeconomic, produced 1,748 vehicles but sold just 1,600 in the first six months of the year.
"Fund managers gave us a figure last year that it needed to sell 15,000 vehicles to breakeven," he said, adding the company has a maximum capacity of 50,000 a year.
Guangzhou Peugeot shareholders made a number of proposals in the last meeting, including changing car models and marketing strategies, and increasing the capital base.
"In the next meeting we will discuss which should be used," he said.
Pan said Denway would continue to diversify and hoped this would help partly offset losses made by Guangzhou Peugeot as the recovery of China's vehicle market would be gradual.

Guangzhou Peugeot also suffered from the erosion of municipal government's favourable policies. The city policy ordered all new taxi license operators to use cars made by the company had been frowned on by central authorities in Beijing.
"I'm not sure whether this policy will be scrapped or not," Pan said.
Under the policy there were already 1,000 Peugeot taxis running in the city since it was fist introduced late last year.
